newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk opposition leader decries corruption.
newsitem.headline: Turk opposition leader decries corruption.

text.p: The main Turkish opposition party leader Mesut Yilmaz called on Turks to resist what he said were links between the state and far-right criminals and demanded corruption in the government be uprooted.
"Politics, guns and dirty money" were together trying to usurp the power of the state, Yilmaz told thousands of supporters on Saturday at an outdoor rally in Istanbul's historic Sultanahmet district.

A fatal car accident on November 3 raised questions about possible ties between the state and gangsters when the passengers turned out to include a senior policeman, a fugitive heroin smuggler and a government MP.
The media is on the trail of allegations that Turkey used a gang of far-right criminals for political killings in exchange for turning a blind eye to their drug trafficking activities.

Former Prime Minister Yilmaz is the head of the Motherland Party, which ruled earlier this year for three months in a coalition with the True Path Party. When the coalition collapsed the True Path Party struck a deal with the Islamists in late June to form the government that is currently in power.
